records.title: Evaluate before choosing vector storage
records.content: The team planned to define evaluation questions and expected evidence before selecting a vector store. Candidates would be compared on retrieval recall, ranking quality, latency, update/delete correctness, operational behavior, and cost.

records.title: Local cosine similarity for notes search
records.content: The team used local cosine similarity for the internal notes search because the corpus had only 120 chunks. The trade-off is that this approach would need an index once the corpus grows to thousands of chunks.

records.title: PostgreSQL full-text search for log search
records.content: The team used PostgreSQL full-text search for the log search prototype because queries were mostly exact error codes and keywords. The trade-off is that it does not match meaning, only words.

records.title: TypeScript for the support assistant API
records.content: The team wrote the support assistant API in TypeScript so the API and the web client could share types. The trade-off is that machine-learning libraries are less mature than in Python.

records.title: No reranker until evaluation shows a need
records.content: The team decided not to add a reranker to the support assistant prototype until evaluation shows that retrieval misses relevant evidence. A reranker has not been built.

records.title: Server-sent events for streaming answers
records.content: The support assistant prototype streams answers to the web client using server-sent events.

records.title: PostgreSQL for the onboarding checklist tool
records.content: The onboarding checklist tool stores its data in PostgreSQL rather than a document database because checklists, items and users have relational links.

records.title: Chunk size for the support assistant
records.content: The support assistant prototype uses a chunk size of 400 tokens. It was chosen after trying 200, 400 and 800 tokens on a small set of queries. There was no formal evaluation.
